cluster_summary: This cluster consists of vulnerabilities in Java and Python libraries where temporary files or directories are created using non-atomic operations (e.g., create, delete, mkdir sequence) that introduce TOCTOU race conditions, or using APIs that default to overly permissive permissions (world-readable), allowing local attackers to read sensitive data or perform symlink attacks. Additional variants include failing to verify permission changes, manually setting overly permissive permissions, and using predictable file names that enable race attacks.
guideline_text: Trace temporary file or directory names created in shared writable locations into manual temporary directory creation sequences such as createTempFile, delete, then mkdir or mkdirs. Report code paths where the temporary path is released between creation and directory creation, allowing another actor to replace or pre-create it before use. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 10 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should use an atomic temporary-directory API such as Files.createTempDirectory and avoid delete-then-mkdir sequences.

mechanism.missing_guard: the temporary path is released between creation and directory creation, allowing another actor to replace or pre-create it before use
mechanism.name: temporary directory create-delete-mkdir TOCTOU race
mechanism.sink_shape: manual temporary directory creation sequences such as createTempFile, delete, then mkdir or mkdirs
mechanism.source_shape: temporary file or directory names created in shared writable locations
mechanism.typical_fix: use an atomic temporary-directory API such as Files.createTempDirectory and avoid delete-then-mkdir sequences

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Replace the non-atomic sequence with a single atomic call to Files.createTempDirectory(), which atomically creates a unique directory with restrictive permissions.
sub_patterns.name: TOCTOU race in temporary directory creation via non-atomic sequence
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code creates a temporary file via File.createTempFile, deletes it, and then creates a directory with the same name via mkdir. This multi-step process is not atomic, allowing an attacker to create a symlink or file between the delete and mkdir operations, leading to insecure temporary directory or arbitrary file write.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Replace File.createTempFile() or File.mkdir() with java.nio.file.Files.createTempFile() or Files.createTempDirectory(), which create files/directories with owner-only permissions (e.g., 0600/0700) by default, or explicitly set restrictive FileAttributes.
sub_patterns.name: Insecure default permissions on temporary files created with legacy Java API
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code uses File.createTempFile() (or File.mkdir()) which creates temporary files/directories with default system-dependent permissions (often world-readable, e.g., 644/755) without enforcing owner-only access, allowing other local users to read sensitive data.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use File.createTempFile(prefix, suffix, directory) to generate a unique, unpredictable filename and set deleteOnExit for cleanup, eliminating the predictability and race window.
sub_patterns.name: Predictable temporary file name leading to TOCTOU race
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code constructs a predictable temporary file name from library name and version and writes to /tmp without atomic creation, allowing a local attacker to create a symlink at the predicted path before the write, leading to arbitrary file write.
